Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: James Cook (author, Wikidata Q7324), died 1779; Joseph Banks (other, Wikidata Q153408), died 1820; John Hawkesworth (editor, Wikidata Q3181710), died 1773. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Cook, James, 1728-1779; Banks, Joseph, 1743-1820 [Contributor]; Hawkesworth, John, 1715?-1773 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The Three Voyages of Captain James Cook Round the World. ..., Printed for Longman , Hurst, Rees, Orme, and Brown, 1821, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/threevoyagescap01cookgoog. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 72%, 68%, 75% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of John Hawkesworth, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
